comment: Integration test: drive a realistic invoice-editing session and assert the grand total (the canary) stays exactly equal to the recomputed sum at every step. A wrong total means some element interfered with another - an observer double-fired, a morph dropped a row, a binding didn't round-trip. Starts: line1 2x500=1000, line2 1x1200=1200, line3 4x75=300 => 2500. Observe fields fire on change (blur/Tab), so edits are committed with Tab.

steps.text: Edit line 1 quantity 2 -> 5 (5x500=2500). Grand total should become 2500-1000+2500 = 4000. One field edit refreshes its line box AND the totals (multi-update _u=linebox-1;totalsPanel).

steps.name: line 2 was NOT disturbed by editing line 1

steps.text: Edit line 3 unit price 75 -> 100 (4x100=400). Grand total 4000-300+400 = 4100. Proves a SECOND independent observe field works alongside the first, no cross-talk.

Add a line (default 1x100=100): grand total 4100+100 = 4200. Add-line is a multi-update refreshing the whole lines container + totals in ONE request; refreshing totalsPanel then fires its AjaxUpdateTrigger, which cascades ONE more request to summaryPanel. So 2 requests total - the update plus the intended dependency cascade - NOT N-per-row. This proves the trigger cascade and multi-update coexist correctly.

steps.name: add line = 1 update + 1 intended trigger cascade (not N-per-row)

steps.text: The earlier edits must SURVIVE the add-line morph: line 1 still 2500, line 3 still 400. If a morph dropped/relabelled a row, these would be wrong.

steps.name: line 1 edit survived the add-line morph
line 3 edit survived the add-line morph (no data jump)

steps.text: Remove line 2 (1200): grand total 4200-1200 = 3000. Removing a row in the MIDDLE is the classic data-jumps-lines hazard; the remaining lines must keep their own totals.

steps.name: line 1 kept its value after a middle row was removed
line 3 kept its value after a middle row was removed

steps.text: Save (AjaxSubmitButton) and confirm the form round-trips without disturbing the total.
